data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 (virtio) is hung: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flapping since ~02:01, so all outbound traffic fails with ENOBUFS even though the interface has a valid IP (198.51.100.27), a correct default route via 198.51.100.1, and the provider side is healthy (modem re-registered, cm_status OPERATIONAL at 02:28). Interface reconfigurations cannot clear the driver hang, so the 4 WAN reloads during this outage had no effect.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 (virtio) is hung: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flapping since ~02:01, so all outbound traffic fails with ENOBUFS even though the interface has a valid IP (198.51.100.27), a correct default route via 198.51.100.1, and the provider side is healthy (modem re-registered, cm_status OPERATIONAL at 02:28). Interface reconfigurations cannot clear the driver hang, so the 4 WAN reloads during this outage had no effect.
evidence: dmesg -a: multiple 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' entries interleaved with 'vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP' — driver queue hangs starting around the outage time.

ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 (the ISP gateway): 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss — transmit path is stuck, not merely filtered; same for 1.1.1.1, and mon.lan also sees 100% loss to 1.1.1.1.
arp -n: entry for the gateway 198.51.100.1 is '(incomplete)' — ARP never resolves because frames never leave the hung NIC.
netstat -i: vtnet0 Oerrs=48211; netstat -s -f inet: '48211 output packets dropped due to no bufs, etc.' — long-running tx failure accumulating since boot (uptime 41 days).
ifconfig -a: vtnet0 UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP with address 198.51.100.27; netstat -rn shows default via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 — addressing/routing are intact, so this is not a lease or route problem.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: outage_start 02:06, reloads at 02:30, 02:40, 02:55, 03:25 all rc=0 with internet still down, then at 03:30 decision 'none' reason 'reload_cap' (12/12 reloads in 24h) — repeated WAN reloads did not restore connectivity.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl: 'Cable Modem Reboot... registration complete' at 02:28 and status OPERATIONAL at 03:00 and 03:30 — the modem/provider side recovered, so the fault is on the firewall's own NIC.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (gw.lan) to reset the hung vtnet0 NIC/driver; a full reboot is needed because four interface reloads during this outage already completed successfully without restoring traffic, which shows reconfiguring the interface does not clear the hang. The maintainer is away and cannot be reached; per policy the reboot may proceed if its conditions hold. Afterwards, consider having the watchdog escalate to a host reboot when reloads stop helping instead of stopping at its 24h reload cap.
